description: Static Fibonacci hot-path cost audit of the ordinary non-LTO, pre-lazy-error-fix runtime.
status: Static CFG/source counts, not dynamic allocation instrumentation or measured time attribution.
formulas: For fib(n), leaves B=F(n+1), internal nodes I=B-1, invocations N=2B-1.
Every invocation calls < once. Each internal invocation additionally calls - twice, fib twice, and + once.
Argument Vecs = N root/recursive fib calls + N comparison calls + 3I arithmetic calls = 2N+3I. Includes each external root fib call.
Local Vecs = N, because every fib closure has one local slot and enter_closure allocates a fresh locals vector.
Eager error Strings = 2B+9I: leaves read one constant/one global; internal nodes read three constants/six globals.
Ordinary non-LTO Rust service calls = 24B+80I. Each reference/push makes three calls; call/test/return make two.
Four inputs (22,23,24,25), each repeated16 times; excludes minor surrounding benchmark loops and checks.

sites.cost: A fresh Rust Vec for every nonempty call, followed by element copying and later deallocation.
A fresh Rust Vec for every Scheme activation with local slots.
Pre-fix code eagerly constructs String error values even for successful accesses. Root changed these to lazy closures after the frozen baseline.
Instruction handlers inline into generated LLVM, but ordinary non-LTO Rust slot/entry services remain separate ABI calls.

limitations: The expression counts establish source-level allocation demand. LLVM may optimize allocation operations; native assembly/profiling must establish surviving physical allocator calls.
Eager String counts refer specifically to the frozen pre-lazy-error-fix runtime hashes, not current source after that fix.
Rust ABI service counts apply to ordinary builds without cross-language LTO. Shared LTO can inline these boundaries.
Counts cover timed recursive Fibonacci subtrees and their incoming root calls, not the benchmark harness, untimed correctness checks, startup, formatting, or occasional collector bookkeeping.
Rust allocator activity is not included in Scheme GC object statistics. These counts do not imply a tracing-GC allocation per call.
No production code changed for this audit. A shared reusable Scheme value stack and frame offsets are the next investigation for eliminating per-call argument/local vectors without type inference.
